claim: The C period is the time between initiation and termination of chromosome replication.
source: The C period is the time between initiation and termination of chromosome replication
evidence: This is a definition provided in the figure caption describing cell cycle periods.

claim: The D period is the time between replication termination and division.
source: the D period is the time between replication termination and division
evidence: This is a definition provided in the figure caption describing cell cycle periods.

claim: The I period is the time between subsequent initiations.
source: the I period is the time between subsequent initiations
evidence: This is a definition provided in the figure caption describing cell cycle periods.

claim: In Escherichia coli, it is controversial whether cell division is tied to chromosome replication or to a replication-independent inter-division process.
source: In Escherichia coli, it is controversial whether cell division is tied to chromosome replication or to a replication-independent inter-division process.
evidence: This statement summarizes the existing controversy in the field as presented in the abstract.

claim: A recent model suggests that both chromosome replication and a replication-independent inter-division process may limit cell division with comparable odds in single cells.
source: A recent model suggests instead that both processes may limit cell division with comparable odds in single cells.
evidence: This refers to a previously published model (concurrent-cycles model) as stated in the abstract.

claim: As a consequence of increased D period, replication became decreasingly limiting for cell division.
source: As a consequence, replication became decreasingly limiting for cell division
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations in the abstract.

claim: Correlations between birth and division are maintained upon width perturbations.
source: correlations between birth and division and between subsequent replication-initiation events were maintained
evidence: This is an experimental observation reported in the abstract.

claim: Correlations between subsequent replication-initiation events are maintained upon width perturbations.
source: correlations between birth and division and between subsequent replication-initiation events were maintained
evidence: This is an experimental observation reported in the abstract.

claim: Both chromosome replication and a replication-independent inter-division process can limit cell division.
source: Our experiments support the hypothesis that both chromosome replication and a replication-independent inter-division process can limit cell division
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study as stated in the abstract.

claim: The two processes have balanced contributions in non-perturbed cells.
source: the two processes have balanced contributions in non-perturbed cells
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data in the abstract.

claim: Width perturbations increase the odds of the replication-independent process being limiting.
source: our width perturbations increase the odds of the replication-independent process being limiting
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data in the abstract.

claim: Temporal regulation of cell division is essential for cellular proliferation in all organisms.
source: Temporal regulation of cell division is essential for cellular proliferation in all organisms.
evidence: This is a general statement based on established biological knowledge.

claim: Timing of cell division determines average cell size in a population of growing cells.
source: Timing of cell division determines average cell size in a population of growing cells
evidence: This is a statement based on established biological principles.

claim: Timing of cell division guarantees that every daughter cell receives one complete copy of chromosomal DNA.
source: Timing of cell division determines average cell size in a population of growing cells and guarantees that every daughter cell receives one complete copy of chromosomal DNA.
evidence: This is a statement based on established biological principles.

claim: The process of division control remains not understood even in the best-studied model system Escherichia coli.
source: Despite its importance, the process remains not understood even in the best-studied model system Escherichia coli.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Three conceptually different classes of models have been proposed to explain division control in E. coli.
source: Three conceptually different classes of models have been proposed to explain division control in E. coli (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This statement refers to existing literature and is illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: According to the first class of models, DNA replication and segregation are regarded as limiting for cell division.
source: According to the first class of models, DNA replication and segregation are regarded as limiting for cell division, while division has no influence on replication.
evidence: This describes one class of models from the literature.

claim: According to the first class of models, division has no influence on replication.
source: According to the first class of models, DNA replication and segregation are regarded as limiting for cell division, while division has no influence on replication.
evidence: This describes one class of models from the literature.

claim: A 'constant' (size-uncoupled) duration since the time of DNA replication initiation (C+D period) has been suggested as a coupling between DNA replication and cell division.
source: At the single-cell level, different couplings between DNA replication and cell division have been suggested: a 'constant' (size-uncoupled) duration since the time of DNA replication initiation (C+D period in Figure 1A; Ho and Amir, 2015; Wallden et al., 2016)
evidence: This describes a specific model from the literature with citations.

claim: The addition of a 'constant' (size-uncoupled) size between replication initiation and division has been suggested as a coupling between DNA replication and cell division.
source: or the addition of a 'constant' (size-uncoupled) size between replication initiation and division (Witz et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes a specific model from the literature with citation.

claim: A second class of models suggests that DNA replication has no direct influence on the timing of cell division under unperturbed growth conditions.
source: A second class of models suggests that DNA replication has no direct influence on the timing of cell division under unperturbed growth conditions (Harris and Theriot, 2016; Harris and Theriot, 2018; Si et al., 2019; Ojkic et al., 2019; Zheng et al., 2020; Ghusinga et al., 2016; Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes a second class of models from the literature with citations.

claim: According to the second class of models, a chromosome-independent process, the accumulation of a molecule or protein, is thought to trigger cell division once copy number reaches a threshold.
source: Instead, a different, chromosome-independent process, the accumulation of a molecule or protein, is thought to trigger cell division, once copy number reaches a threshold.
evidence: This describes the mechanism proposed by the second class of models.

claim: The size added by cells between birth and division is independent of their size at birth.
source: Evidence comes from the observation that the size added by cells between birth and division is independent of their size at birth (Campos et al., 2014; Taheri-Araghi et al., 2015; Amir, 2014).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature supporting the second class of models.

claim: Experiments demonstrate the independence of 'adder' behavior from perturbations of DNA replication.
source: Further evidence comes from experiments that demonstrate the independence of this 'adder' behavior from perturbations of DNA replication (Si et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature supporting the second class of models.

claim: Cell-wall precursor molecules have been suggested as accumulator molecules for division control.
source: Different 'accumulator' molecules have been suggested – notably cell-wall precursor molecules (Harris and Theriot, 2016)
evidence: This is a hypothesis from cited literature.

claim: Components of the divisome or septum have been suggested as accumulator molecules for division control.
source: components of the divisome or septum (Zheng et al., 2020)
evidence: This is a hypothesis from cited literature.

claim: FtsZ proteins have been suggested as accumulator molecules for division control.
source: or, more specifically, FtsZ proteins (Si et al., 2019; Ojkic et al., 2019; Serbanescu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from cited literature.

claim: Whether cells effectively measure a constant size increase remains controversial.
source: However, whether cells effectively measure a constant size increase, whether the adder behavior emerges through the accumulation of a single molecule, and/or whether chromosome replication/segregation have a direct influence on cell division remains controversial (Witz et al., 2019; Si et al., 2019; Zheng et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement describes ongoing controversy in the field with citations.

claim: Whether the adder behavior emerges through the accumulation of a single molecule remains controversial.
source: However, whether cells effectively measure a constant size increase, whether the adder behavior emerges through the accumulation of a single molecule, and/or whether chromosome replication/segregation have a direct influence on cell division remains controversial (Witz et al., 2019; Si et al., 2019; Zheng et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement describes ongoing controversy in the field with citations.

claim: Whether chromosome replication/segregation have a direct influence on cell division remains controversial.
source: However, whether cells effectively measure a constant size increase, whether the adder behavior emerges through the accumulation of a single molecule, and/or whether chromosome replication/segregation have a direct influence on cell division remains controversial (Witz et al., 2019; Si et al., 2019; Zheng et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement describes ongoing controversy in the field with citations.

claim: The concurrent-cycles model proposes that two processes limit cell division: DNA replication/segregation and a second 'inter-division' process.
source: A third model developed by some of us proposes that two processes limit cell division, DNA replication/segregation and a second 'inter-division' process that relates cell size at division to cell size at birth, independently of DNA replication or segregation (Micali et al., 2018b; Figure 1C).
evidence: This describes the concurrent-cycles model with citation.

claim: The inter-division process relates cell size at division to cell size at birth, independently of DNA replication or segregation.
source: A third model developed by some of us proposes that two processes limit cell division, DNA replication/segregation and a second 'inter-division' process that relates cell size at division to cell size at birth, independently of DNA replication or segregation (Micali et al., 2018b; Figure 1C).
evidence: This describes a feature of the concurrent-cycles model with citation.

claim: According to the concurrent-cycles model, the slowest process sets the timing of cell division at the single-cell level.
source: According to this 'concurrent-cycles' model, the slowest process sets the timing of cell division at the single-cell level.
evidence: This describes a key feature of the concurrent-cycles model.

claim: DNA-replication initiation is controlled through an adder-like process between subsequent initiation events.
source: Based on recent experimental evidence (Si et al., 2019; Witz et al., 2019), DNA-replication initiation is controlled through an adder-like process between subsequent initiation events
evidence: This is based on experimental evidence from cited literature.

claim: The adder-like process for replication initiation could stem from a molecule accumulating during replication events.
source: which could also stem from a molecule accumulating during replication events (Ho and Amir, 2015; Sompayrac and Maaloe, 1973).
evidence: This is a hypothesis from cited literature.

claim: Single-cycle models fail to explain experimental data on the B and C+D subperiods in single cells.
source: Micali et al. showed that single-cycle models proposed (Wallden et al., 2016; Ho and Amir, 2015; Harris and Theriot, 2016) fail to explain experimental data on the B and C+D subperiods in single cells
evidence: This is a conclusion from a cited study.

claim: The concurrent-cycles model is able to fit previously available experimental datasets.
source: while the concurrent-cycles model is able to fit the previously available experimental datasets (Micali et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is a conclusion from a cited study.

claim: The concurrent-cycles model has more fit parameters than any of the more simple previous models.
source: However, the model makes assumptions about the nature of the underlying processes and has more fit parameters than any of the more simple previous models.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation of the concurrent-cycles model.

claim: Increasing cell width through titration of the MreB-actin cytoskeleton causes an increase of the period between replication termination and cell division (D period).
source: Zheng et al., 2016 showed that increasing cell width through titration of the MreB-actin cytoskeleton causes an increase of the period between replication termination and cell division (D period)
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature.

claim: Increasing cell width through titration of the MreB-actin cytoskeleton does not affect the average duration of DNA replication (C period).
source: Zheng et al., 2016 showed that increasing cell width through titration of the MreB-actin cytoskeleton causes an increase of the period between replication termination and cell division (D period) without affecting the average duration of DNA replication (C period)
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature.

claim: Increasing cell width through titration of the MreB-actin cytoskeleton does not affect cell-cycle duration.
source: Zheng et al., 2016 showed that increasing cell width through titration of the MreB-actin cytoskeleton causes an increase of the period between replication termination and cell division (D period) without affecting the average duration of DNA replication (C period) or cell-cycle duration (see also Si et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature.

claim: An increased D period might correspond to a decreasingly limiting role of DNA replication for cell division.
source: We hypothesized, that an increased D period might correspond to a decreasingly limiting role of DNA replication and an increasingly limiting role of the inter-division process for cell division.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: An increased D period might correspond to an increasingly limiting role of the inter-division process for cell division.
source: We hypothesized, that an increased D period might correspond to a decreasingly limiting role of DNA replication and an increasingly limiting role of the inter-division process for cell division.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: The authors systematically increased cell width through perturbations of the MreB actin cytoskeleton.
source: Similar to Zheng et al., 2016, we thus systematically increased cell width through perturbations of the MreB actin cytoskeleton.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: The authors followed single-cell division and DNA replication in microfluidic devices during steady-state growth conditions in minimal media.
source: We then followed single-cell division and DNA replication in microfluidic devices during steady-state growth conditions in minimal media, similar to previous work (Wallden et al., 2016; Si et al., 2019; Witz et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Upon increasing D period, cell size at division showed continuously decreasing correlations with cell size at initiation of DNA replication.
source: Indeed, upon increasing D period, cell size at division showed continuously decreasing correlations with cell size at initiation of DNA replication.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from the study.

claim: In non-perturbed cells, DNA replication appears to have an important limiting role, as supported by high correlations between division size and size at replication initiation.
source: On the contrary, in non-perturbed cells, DNA replication appears to have an important limiting role, as supported by the high correlations between division size and size at replication initiation also observed previously (Witz et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental data with citation to previous work.

claim: Only the concurrent-process model is able to describe the experimental data in both perturbed and unperturbed conditions.
source: By testing two recently proposed single-process models (Si et al., 2019; Witz et al., 2019) and the concurrent-process model from Micali et al., we found that only the concurrent-process model is able to describe the experimental data in both perturbed and unperturbed conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from model testing against experimental data.

claim: Cell division is controlled by at least two concurrent processes that link cell division to DNA replication and cell birth, respectively.
source: In summary, our work suggests that cell division is controlled by at least two concurrent processes that link cell division to DNA replication and cell birth, respectively.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: The modified wildtype strain used is NCM3722, λ::P127-mcherry, dnaN::Ypet-dnaN.
source: To investigate division control in the model organism E. coli, we measured cell division and DNA replication at the single-cell level using a modified wildtype strain (NCM3722, λ::P127-mcherry, dnaN::Ypet-dnaN)
evidence: This describes the bacterial strain used in the study.

claim: The strain contains a cytoplasmic mCherry marker for accurate measurements of cell dimensions.
source: which contains a cytoplasmic mCherry marker for accurate measurements of cell dimensions
evidence: This describes a feature of the bacterial strain used in the study.

claim: The strain contains a functional fluorescent-protein fusion to the beta-clamp of the DNA-replication machinery (YPet-DnaN), introduced at the native dnaN locus.
source: and a functional fluorescent-protein fusion to the beta-clamp of the DNA-replication machinery (YPet-DnaN), introduced at the native dnaN locus (Reyes-Lamothe et al., 2010).
evidence: This describes a feature of the bacterial strain used in the study with citation.

claim: The YPet-DnaN fusion forms foci at the replication fork during DNA replication but is diffuse otherwise.
source: The YPet-DnaN fusion forms foci at the replication fork during DNA replication but is diffuse otherwise (Figure 2A; Reyes-Lamothe et al., 2010; Moolman et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the behavior of the fluorescent marker with citations and reference to figure.

claim: Cells were grown in microfluidic devices commonly referred to as 'mother machines'.
source: To investigate cells during exponential, steady-state growth conditions, we grew cells in microfluidic devices commonly referred to as 'mother machines' (Figure 2A, Figure 2—video 1), similar to previous experiments (Wang et al., 2010; Long et al., 2013; Long et al., 2014; Si et al., 2019; Witz et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the experimental setup with citations.

claim: Cells were grown in minimal medium (M9+NH4Cl+glycerol) to reliably distinguish subsequent rounds of DNA replication.
source: To reliably distinguish subsequent rounds of DNA replication, we grew cells in minimal medium (M9+NH4Cl+glycerol), such that subsequent replication rounds do not overlap.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions and rationale.

claim: In minimal medium (M9+NH4Cl+glycerol), subsequent replication rounds do not overlap.
source: To reliably distinguish subsequent rounds of DNA replication, we grew cells in minimal medium (M9+NH4Cl+glycerol), such that subsequent replication rounds do not overlap.
evidence: This describes a consequence of the experimental conditions.

claim: In unperturbed cells, the average C period is 51±1 min.
source: In unperturbed cells, we found an average C period of 51±1 min and a D period of 22±4 min (Supplementary file 1), in agreement with previous bulk measurements (Michelsen et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an experimental measurement from the study with citation to previous work.

claim: In unperturbed cells, the average D period is 22±4 min.
source: In unperturbed cells, we found an average C period of 51±1 min and a D period of 22±4 min (Supplementary file 1), in agreement with previous bulk measurements (Michelsen et al., 2003).
evidence: This is an experimental measurement from the study with citation to previous work.

claim: DnaN stays bound to DNA for about 5 min after replication termination.
source: Since DnaN stays bound to DNA for about 5 min after replication termination (Moolman et al., 2014), we likely overestimate the average C period and underestimate the D period by this amount.
evidence: This is a known property of DnaN from cited literature.

claim: The authors likely overestimate the average C period by about 5 min.
source: Since DnaN stays bound to DNA for about 5 min after replication termination (Moolman et al., 2014), we likely overestimate the average C period and underestimate the D period by this amount.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a potential measurement bias.

claim: The authors likely underestimate the average D period by about 5 min.
source: Since DnaN stays bound to DNA for about 5 min after replication termination (Moolman et al., 2014), we likely overestimate the average C period and underestimate the D period by this amount.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a potential measurement bias.

claim: The absolute change of period durations does not affect investigations of cell-cycle regulation based on the combined C+D period.
source: However, this absolute change of period durations does not affect our investigations of cell-cycle regulation, which are based on the combined C+D period.
evidence: This is a statement about the impact of measurement bias on the study's conclusions.

claim: The authors systematically increased cell width by perturbing the MreB-actin cytoskeleton.
source: Based on previous work by Zheng et al., 2016, we therefore systematically increased cell width by perturbing the MreB-actin cytoskeleton (Figure 2B).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach with citation and reference to figure.

claim: The authors treated cells with sub-inhibitory concentrations of the MreB-polymerization inhibitor A22.
source: Instead of titrating MreB levels (Zheng et al., 2016), we treated cells with sub-inhibitory concentrations of the MreB-polymerization inhibitor A22 (Bean et al., 2009), similar to previous studies (Tropini et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach with citations.

claim: Increasing A22 concentration leads to increasing steady-state cell width both in batch culture and in the mother machine.
source: Increasing A22 concentration leads to increasing steady-state cell width both in batch culture and in the mother machine (Figure 2B)
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: Increasing A22 concentration does not affect cell-to-cell width fluctuations.
source: Increasing A22 concentration leads to increasing steady-state cell width both in batch culture and in the mother machine (Figure 2B), without affecting cell-to-cell width fluctuations (Figure 2—figure supplement 2)
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: Increasing A22 concentration does not affect doubling time.
source: without affecting cell-to-cell width fluctuations (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), and without affecting doubling time (Figure 2C)
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: Increasing A22 concentration does not affect single-cell growth rate.
source: and without affecting doubling time (Figure 2C) or single-cell growth rate (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: Growth-rate fluctuations remain constant with increasing A22 concentration.
source: Furthermore, growth-rate fluctuations remain constant (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A) and similar to previous measurements (Kennard et al., 2016; Grilli et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure and citations.

claim: The increase of cell width leads to an increase in the average D period.
source: In line with the results of Zheng et al., 2016, the increase of cell width leads to an increase in the average D period (Figure 2C) as hypothesized.
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure and citation.

claim: The average C period remains unperturbed with increasing cell width.
source: At the same time, the average C period (Figure 2C) and the average cell volume at the time of replication initiation remain unperturbed (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), as previously reported (Zheng et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figures and citation.

claim: The average cell volume at the time of replication initiation remains unperturbed with increasing cell width.
source: At the same time, the average C period (Figure 2C) and the average cell volume at the time of replication initiation remain unperturbed (Figure 2—figure supplement 5), as previously reported (Zheng et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figures and citation.

claim: Cell-to-cell fluctuations in the duration of I, C, and interdivision periods remain constant with increasing cell width.
source: Cell-to-cell fluctuations in the duration of sub-periods remain constant (I, C, and interdivision periods) or decrease mildly (D period) (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: Cell-to-cell fluctuations in the duration of the D period decrease mildly with increasing cell width.
source: Cell-to-cell fluctuations in the duration of sub-periods remain constant (I, C, and interdivision periods) or decrease mildly (D period) (Figure 2—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: The shift of replication to earlier times is observed in the probability distributions of replicase positions.
source: While sub-periods are extracted from single-cell lineages, the shift of replication to earlier times is also observed in the probability distributions of replicase positions (Figure 2D)
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: With increasing D period duration, cells continued to show near-adder behavior with a weak trend towards sizer behavior.
source: With increasing D period duration (through increasing A22 concentration), cells continued to show near-adder behavior with a weak trend towards sizer behavior (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: Cells show adder behavior between subsequent rounds of replication initiation.
source: Similarly, cells also show adder behavior between subsequent rounds of replication initiation (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: The adder behavior between subsequent initiations is robust with respect to variations of average growth rate using a poorer growth medium.
source: This behavior is robust with respect to variations of average growth rate using a poorer growth medium (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: The average size per origin and average added size per origin are equal to one another during steady-state growth.
source: Ho and Amir, 2015 previously demonstrated that the average size per origin and average added size per origin are equal to one another during steady-state growth.
evidence: This is a theoretical result from cited literature.

claim: The scaling of average cell size at initiation with the number of replication origins was initially deduced by Donachie, 1968.
source: The scaling of average cell size at initiation with the number of replication origins initially deduced by Donachie, 1968 and later confirmed for different growth rates (Wallden et al., 2016) and for different cell widths (Zheng et al., 2020)
evidence: This is a historical observation from cited literature.

claim: The scaling of average cell size at initiation with the number of replication origins was confirmed for different growth rates.
source: The scaling of average cell size at initiation with the number of replication origins initially deduced by Donachie, 1968 and later confirmed for different growth rates (Wallden et al., 2016) and for different cell widths (Zheng et al., 2020)
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature.

claim: The scaling of average cell size at initiation with the number of replication origins was confirmed for different cell widths.
source: The scaling of average cell size at initiation with the number of replication origins initially deduced by Donachie, 1968 and later confirmed for different growth rates (Wallden et al., 2016) and for different cell widths (Zheng et al., 2020)
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature.

claim: ζI is constant, independently of A22 treatment.
source: We found that ζI is constant, independently of A22 treatment (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: The constancy of ζI and the constancy of the average initiation volume suggest that the process of replication initiation is not affected by A22-induced cell widening.
source: Together with the constancy of the average initiation volume (Figure 2—figure supplement 5, Ho and Amir, 2015; Si et al., 2017; Zheng et al., 2016) this suggests that the process of replication initiation is not affected by the A22-induced cell widening.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations with citations.

claim: Correlations between initiation size and corresponding cell division systematically change as a function of average D period.
source: In contrast to the weak dependency of ζG and ζI on drug treatment, correlations between initiation size and corresponding cell division systematically change as a function of average D period (Figure 3G–H).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figures.

claim: ζCD continuously changes toward a value of -1 with increasing average D period.
source: ζCD continuously changes toward a value of -1 with increasing average D period (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: The negative value of ζCD corresponds to a lack of correlation between division size and size at initiation.
source: Note that the negative value of ζCD corresponds to a lack of correlation between division size and size at initiation (Figure 3G), typically predicted by the models where replication is never limiting for cell division Micali et al., 2018b; Si et al., 2019.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental observation with citations.

claim: Division size is decreasingly dependent of the size at initiation with increasing D period.
source: This lack of correlations can also be illustrated differently: Division size is decreasingly dependent of the size at initiation with increasing D period (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: With increasing average D period, replication is increasingly likely to happen in the mother cell.
source: With increasing average D period, replication is increasingly likely to happen in the mother cell (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: The spread of the C period over a division event does not affect correlations between initiation and division or between subsequent initiation events.
source: We did not observe a separation of point clouds nor differences between their slopes, suggesting that the spread of the C period over a division event does not affect correlations between initiation and division or between subsequent initiation events.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations.

claim: With increasing average D period, a process different from DNA replication is likely increasingly responsible for division control.
source: From these observations, we conclude that with increasing average D period a process different from DNA replication is likely increasingly responsible for division control.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations.

claim: The concurrent-cycles model assumes two processes that must both finish for cell division to occur.
source: The model assumes two processes that must both finish for cell division to occur, one replication/segregation process related to the size at replication initiation and one inter-division process related to the size at birth.
evidence: This describes the concurrent-cycles model.

claim: The concurrent-cycles model contains three control parameters: ζCD', ζH, and ζI.
source: The model contains three control parameters: ζCD′ controls the replication/segregation process and ζH controls the inter-division process. A third parameter, ζI controls the inter-initiation process that relates replication initiation to the cell size at the previous initiation.
evidence: This describes the parameters of the concurrent-cycles model.

claim: In the concurrent-cycles model, the slopes of the inter-division period (ζG) and of the C+D period (ζCD) emerge from the competition of the two cycles and are predictions of the model.
source: The slopes of the inter-division period (ζG) and of the C+D period (ζCD) emerge from the competition of the two cycles and are predictions of the model.
evidence: This describes predictions of the concurrent-cycles model.

claim: The inter-initiation process is set to be an adder (ζI=0) based on experimental results.
source: To fit the concurrent-cycles model to our experimental data, we set the inter-initiation process to be an adder (ζI=0), based on our experimental results (Figure 3C), in agreement with previous observations in unperturbed cells (Si et al., 2019; Witz et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes a model assumption based on experimental data with citations.

claim: Replication segregation (the C+D' period) is assumed to be a timer process (ζCD'=1) in the concurrent-cycles model.
source: Furthermore, we assumed that replication segregation (the C+D' perid) is a timer process (ζCD′=1) that requires a minimum time to be completed, which is independent of size at the time of initiation, and does not vary in A22 perturbations.
evidence: This describes a model assumption.

claim: For the inter-division process, the concurrent-cycles model assumes ζH=0 (adder).
source: For the inter-division process we assumed that ζH=0 (adder).
evidence: This describes a model assumption.

claim: The adder hypothesis for the inter-division process is compatible with the accumulation models of FtsZ or other divisome/septum components.
source: The adder hypothesis is also compatible with the accumulation models of FtsZ or other divisome/septum components for this sub-period, as recently hypothesized Si et al., 2019; Zheng et al., 2020; Ojkic et al., 2019.
evidence: This is a statement about the compatibility of the model assumption with other hypotheses from cited literature.

claim: The parameter pH quantifies the probability that the inter-division process is limiting.
source: Compared to a single-process model, this framework outputs the extra parameter pH, which quantifies the probability that the inter-division process is limiting.
evidence: This describes an output parameter of the concurrent-cycles model.

claim: Increasing D period duration leads to an increase of pH.
source: Figure 4B shows how by fitting the model to our data, increasing D period duration leads to an increase of pH.
evidence: This is a result from model fitting to experimental data with reference to figure.

claim: The two independent processes, DNA replication and a replication-independent inter-division process, are almost equally likely to limit cell division under unperturbed conditions.
source: The model therefore predicts that the two independent processes, DNA replication and a replication-independent inter-division process, are almost equally likely to limit cell division under unperturbed conditions (Micali et al., 2018b).
evidence: This is a prediction from the concurrent-cycles model with citation.

claim: With increasing average D period through perturbation by A22, the replication-independent inter-division process is increasingly likely limiting for cell division.
source: However, with increasing average D period through perturbation by A22, the replication-independent inter-division process is increasingly likely limiting for cell division.
evidence: This is a prediction from the concurrent-cycles model fitted to experimental data.

claim: Both single-process models (Si et al., 2019 and Witz et al., 2019) appear to be incompatible with the experimental data.
source: We found that both frameworks appear to be incompatible with our data (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a conclusion from model testing against experimental data with reference to figure.

claim: pH≈0.5 at slow growth (if the average doubling time is smaller than 1.4 hr).
source: Interestingly, when fitting our model to all datasets including our own, we found that pH≈0.5 at slow growth (if the average doubling time is smaller than 1.4 hr), while pH increases with decreasing doubling time.
evidence: This is a result from model fitting to multiple datasets.

claim: pH increases with decreasing doubling time.
source: Interestingly, when fitting our model to all datasets including our own, we found that pH≈0.5 at slow growth (if the average doubling time is smaller than 1.4 hr), while pH increases with decreasing doubling time.
evidence: This is a result from model fitting to multiple datasets.

claim: The trend of increasing pH with decreasing doubling time is in qualitative agreement with recent work from Tiruvadi-Krishnan et al., 2021.
source: This trend is in qualitative agreement with recent work from Tiruvadi-Krishnan et al., 2021, who propose that DNA replication limits division at slow growth but not at fast growth (see also Discussion).
evidence: This is a comparison with findings from cited literature.

claim: Cells control the timing of cell division based on at least two processes in slow-growth conditions: genome replication/segregation and an inter-division process.
source: In conclusion, our study suggests that cells control the timing of cell division based on at least two processes in slow-growth conditions: genome replication/segregation and an inter-division process, which relates cell division to size at birth.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: The inter-division process relates cell division to size at birth.
source: In conclusion, our study suggests that cells control the timing of cell division based on at least two processes in slow-growth conditions: genome replication/segregation and an inter-division process, which relates cell division to size at birth.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: Experimental data obtained in this study and in previous studies are well described by the concurrent-cycles model.
source: Accordingly, experimental data obtained in this study and in previous studies are well described by the concurrent-cycles model, while the available single-process models fail to describe our experimental data in unperturbed and perturbed conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from model testing against experimental data.

claim: The available single-process models fail to describe experimental data in unperturbed and perturbed conditions.
source: Accordingly, experimental data obtained in this study and in previous studies are well described by the concurrent-cycles model, while the available single-process models fail to describe our experimental data in unperturbed and perturbed conditions.
evidence: This is a conclusion from model testing against experimental data.

claim: Cell size at division and cell size at initiation of DNA replication are correlated in unperturbed cells (ζCD=0).
source: First, cell size at division and cell size at initiation of DNA replication are correlated in unperturbed cells (ζCD=0, Figure 3), as already observed previously (Micali et al., 2018b; Witz et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure and citations.

claim: Division and replication cannot proceed fully independently of one another.
source: Thus, division and replication cannot proceed fully independently of one another, as previously suggested (Si et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations with citation.

claim: When increasing cell width and the average D period with A22, decreasing correlations between DNA replication and division were observed (a decrease of ζCD towards -1).
source: When increasing cell width and the average D period with A22, we observed decreasing correlations between DNA replication and division (a decrease of ζCD towards -1) (Figure 3)
evidence: This is an experimental observation with reference to figure.

claim: Division becomes decreasingly dependent of replication with increasing cell width and D period.
source: which suggests that division becomes decreasingly dependent of replication.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations.

claim: Two key cell-cycle couplings remained nearly unchanged (ζG≈0, ζI≈0) with increasing cell width and D period.
source: At the same time, two other key cell-cycle couplings remained nearly unchanged (ζG≈0, ζI≈0).
evidence: This is an experimental observation.

claim: The data are in line with the idea that a replication-independent process related to size at birth contributes to division control.
source: Our data are in line with the idea that a replication-independent process related to size at birth contributes to division control, and that this process is dominant upon width perturbations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations.

claim: The replication-independent process is dominant upon width perturbations.
source: Our data are in line with the idea that a replication-independent process related to size at birth contributes to division control, and that this process is dominant upon width perturbations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations.

claim: Cell division is apparently affected by both cell size at birth and DNA replication.
source: Thus, cell division is apparently affected by both cell size at birth and DNA replication.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations.

claim: The concurrent-cycles model suggests that the inter-division process is an adder-like process (ζH≈0).
source: The concurrent-cycles model suggests that the inter-division process is an adder-like process (ζH≈0), which shows a mild trend toward sizer with increasing perturbation.
evidence: This is a result from model fitting.

claim: The inter-division process shows a mild trend toward sizer with increasing perturbation.
source: The concurrent-cycles model suggests that the inter-division process is an adder-like process (ζH≈0), which shows a mild trend toward sizer with increasing perturbation.
evidence: This is a result from model fitting.

claim: The adder-like nature of the inter-division process is supported by experiments with dividing filamentous cells.
source: The adder-like nature of this process is also supported by experiments with dividing filamentous cells, where DNA replication is likely never limiting cell division (Wehrens et al., 2018).
evidence: This is support from cited experimental work.

claim: Multiple studies suggested that cells divide independently of DNA replication, based on a licensing molecule that accumulates since birth.
source: Recently, multiple studies suggested that cells divide independently of DNA replication, based on a licensing molecule that accumulates since birth and reaches a critical threshold in copy number at the time of cell septation or division (Si et al., 2019; Zheng et al., 2020; Ojkic et al., 2019; Harris and Theriot, 2016; Panlilio et al., 2021).
evidence: This summarizes hypotheses from cited literature.

claim: The licensing molecule reaches a critical threshold in copy number at the time of cell septation or division.
source: Recently, multiple studies suggested that cells divide independently of DNA replication, based on a licensing molecule that accumulates since birth and reaches a critical threshold in copy number at the time of cell septation or division (Si et al., 2019; Zheng et al., 2020; Ojkic et al., 2019; Harris and Theriot, 2016; Panlilio et al., 2021).
evidence: This summarizes hypotheses from cited literature.

claim: The peptidoglycan accumulation model is based on the assumption that peptidoglycan accumulates in proportion to cell volume.
source: The peptidoglycan accumulation model is based on the assumption that peptidoglycan accumulates in proportion to cell volume, while cell-wall insertion occurs in proportion to cell-surface growth.
evidence: This describes a model from the literature.

claim: Cell surface area grows in proportion to biomass.
source: However, some of us recently demonstrated that cell surface area grows in proportion to biomass (Oldewurtel et al., 2021)
evidence: This is an experimental finding from cited work.

claim: It is more likely that peptidoglycan synthesis and cell-wall insertion happen at equal rates.
source: which makes it more likely that peptidoglycan synthesis and cell-wall insertion happen at equal rates.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from cited experimental work.

claim: Cell size at z-ring formation correlates with total FtsZ abundance (rather than FtsZ concentration).
source: Cell size at z-ring formation correlates with total FtsZ abundance (rather than FtsZ concentration) (Männik et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature.

claim: Controlled repression or over-expression of FtsZ delay or accelerate subsequent cell division.
source: Furthermore, controlled repression or over-expression of FtsZ delay or accelerate subsequent cell division (Si et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature.

claim: The expression of FtsZ is cell-cycle dependent.
source: However, at the same time, the expression of FtsZ is cell-cycle dependent (Männik et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature.

claim: Whether the accumulation of FtsZ or other divisome components are responsible for an adder-like inter-division process requires further investigation.
source: Whether the accumulation of FtsZ or other divisome components are responsible for an adder-like inter-division process thus requires further investigation.
evidence: This is a statement about the need for future research.

claim: Z-ring formation and DNA segregation are coupled through the processes of nucleoid occlusion.
source: Z-ring formation and DNA segregation are coupled through the processes of nucleoid occlusion, which inhibits Z-ring formation on top of nucleoids, and ter linkage, a process that links the Z-ring to the terminal region of the segregated chromosomes (Dewachter et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited literature.

claim: Nucleoid occlusion inhibits Z-ring formation on top of nucleoids.
source: Z-ring formation and DNA segregation are coupled through the processes of nucleoid occlusion, which inhibits Z-ring formation on top of nucleoids
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited literature.

claim: Ter linkage is a process that links the Z-ring to the terminal region of the segregated chromosomes.
source: and ter linkage, a process that links the Z-ring to the terminal region of the segregated chromosomes (Dewachter et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge from cited literature.

claim: FtsZ-protein expression increases in a step-wise manner during the cell cycle.
source: Another link in slow-growth conditions comes from FtsZ expression: FtsZ-protein expression increases in a step-wise manner during the cell cycle (Männik et al., 2018)
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature.

claim: Z-ring formation happens predominantly after the increase of FtsZ production.
source: and Z-ring formation happens predominantly after the increase of production (Männik et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature.

claim: Which process is coupling the timing of replication to division remains to be determined.
source: However, which of these or other processes is coupling the timing of replication to division remains to be determined.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: Inter-division and DNA replication/segregation processes are equally likely limiting cell division (pH≈0.5) in two different minimal growth media.
source: Based on the concurrent-cycles model, we predict that inter-division and DNA replication/segregation processes are equally likely limiting cell division (pH≈0.5) in two different minimal growth media (Figure 4—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This is a prediction from the concurrent-cycles model with reference to figure.

claim: The same balance (pH≈0.5) was previously reported for previous experiments at slow growth.
source: and we previously reported the same balance (Micali et al., 2018b) for previous experiments at slow growth (Adiciptaningrum et al., 2016; Wallden et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a result from previous work with citations.

claim: Temporal correlations between replication termination and z-ring constriction are high at slow growth.
source: They demonstrate that temporal correlations between replication termination and z-ring constriction are high at slow growth, which supports a limiting role of DNA replication for cell division
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature.

claim: Temporal correlations between replication termination and z-ring constriction decrease at fast growth.
source: but correlations decrease at fast growth, which then requires a different process to control cell division, in qualitative agreement with the concurrent-cycles model (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cited literature with reference to figure.

claim: The balance between the replication/segregation and inter-division processes at slow growth is surprising.
source: The balance between the replication/segregation and inter-division processes at slow growth, over a broad regime of growth rates, is surprising, as it requires that both processes terminate, on average, at the same cell volume 2⟨V0⟩.
evidence: This is a statement about the implications of the findings.

claim: With ΔI constant, ΔH must scale in proportion to 2[(C+D′)/τ]≈2[(C+D)/τ].
source: With ΔI constant, ΔH must therefore scale in proportion to 2[(C+D′)/τ]≈2[(C+D)/τ].
evidence: This is a theoretical inference.

claim: It was previously thought that cell size increases exponentially with growth rate.
source: While it was previously thought that cell size increases exponentially with growth rate (Schaechter et al., 1958), Zheng et al., 2020 identified a linear relationship.
evidence: This is a historical statement about previous understanding with citation.

claim: Zheng et al., 2020 identified a linear relationship between cell size and growth rate.
source: While it was previously thought that cell size increases exponentially with growth rate (Schaechter et al., 1958), Zheng et al., 2020 identified a linear relationship.
evidence: This is an experimental finding from cited literature.

claim: Zheng et al., 2020 suggested an accumulator model that could reconcile the growth-rate dependent increase of average cell size if the threshold molecule was produced at a rate proportional to 1/(C+D) on average.
source: Based on these experimental findings, they suggested an accumulator model (equivalent to our H-process) that could reconcile the growth-rate dependent increase of average cell size, as long as the threshold molecule was produced at a rate proportional to 1/(C+D) on average.
evidence: This is a hypothesis from cited literature.

claim: Recent theoretical work supports the relationship between threshold molecule production rate and 1/(C+D) based on the assumption of constitutive divisor expression.
source: Recent theoretical work supports this relationship (Serbanescu et al., 2020) based on the assumption of constitutive divisor expression.
evidence: This is a theoretical result from cited literature.

claim: The assumption of constitutive divisor expression finds some experimental validation from nutrient-shift data.
source: The same assumption also finds some experimental validation from nutrient-shift data (Panlilio et al., 2021).
evidence: This is experimental support from cited literature.

claim: Constitutive divisor-protein expression could provide an explanation for the maintenance of pH over different unperturbed conditions.
source: Constitutive divisor-protein expression could provide an explanation for the maintenance of pH over different unperturbed conditions.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: As soon as only one of the two processes is modulated, their balance is broken.
source: However, as soon as only one of the two processes is modulated, for example through width perturbations (Figure 4), their balance is broken.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from experimental observations with reference to figure.

claim: Tiruvadi-Krishnan et al., 2021 suggest that a checkpoint temporally close to DNA replication solely limits the timing of z-ring constriction at slow growth but not at fast growth.
source: While they do not put forward a complete cell-cycle model, they suggest that a checkpoint temporally close to DNA replication solely limits the timing of z-ring constriction and therefore cell division at slow growth but not at fast growth.
evidence: This is a hypothesis from cited literature.

claim: The concurrent-cycles framework assumes that replication initiation is independent of cell division or cell size at birth.
source: The concurrent-cycles framework assumes that replication initiation is independent of cell division or cell size at birth, based on the robust measurements of adder behavior between subsequent initiations (Figure 3C).
evidence: This describes an assumption of the concurrent-cycles model with reference to figure.

claim: DNA replication may not be entirely independent of cell division.
source: However, we note that this is not the only possibility, and DNA replication may not be entirely independent of cell division.
evidence: This is a statement acknowledging alternative possibilities.

claim: A complementary hypothesis posits a possible connection of initiation to the preceding division event.
source: A complementary hypothesis (Kleckner et al., 2018) posits a possible (additional or complementary) connection of initiation to the preceding division event.
evidence: This is a hypothesis from cited literature.

claim: Cell-cycle regulation remains to be understood mechanistically.
source: In conclusion, cell-cycle regulation remains to be understood mechanistically.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: In standard conditions both DNA replication and cell growth since birth play important roles for division timing.
source: However, from our work it appears that in standard conditions both DNA replication and cell growth since birth play important roles for division timing.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.
